evidence.text: The opened page identifies the displayed form as the Shuowen small-seal form of 很 and gives references to the Shuowen and later dictionaries. It does not show an earlier oracle-bone, bronze, or Warring States form, so it supports a small-seal-stage candidate rather than a continuous graphic sequence.

evidence.text: The entry analyzes 很 as a phono-semantic compound with semantic 彳 and phonetic 艮. In Zhengzhang Shangfang’s 2003 Old Chinese reconstruction, 很 is *ɡɯːnʔ and 艮 is *kɯːns; the same source lists Standard Mandarin hěn and Cantonese Jyutping han2 for 很. The historical forms are similar enough to support a phonetic relationship in that reconstruction, but are not identical. The entry does not establish a semantic derivation from the oldest meaning of 艮.
evidence.title: 很 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.text: For 艮, the entry gives Mandarin gèn and Zhengzhang’s 2003 Old Chinese *kɯːns. These readings provide a same-system comparison with 很 *ɡɯːnʔ. This supports 艮 as a sound component; it does not establish the original referent or name behind 艮’s own graph.
evidence.title: 艮 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.text: The entry quotes 很 in transmitted passages attributed to the Zhuangzi (dated there circa 3rd–2nd centuries BCE), the Book of Rites (circa 4th–2nd centuries BCE), and the Mencius (circa 4th century BCE). The quoted contexts use 很 for querulousness or defiance, disputes, and fighting/violence, not as the modern degree adverb. These dates describe the cited works; the entry is not a manuscript witness and the date of a work does not by itself date the surviving wording.
evidence.title: 很 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.text: The accessible abstract of this 2024 article proposes that the modern degree adverb derives from Yuan northern Chinese–Mongolian contact and an earlier degree use written 哏; it describes later written spellings as 狠 in some Ming texts and mixed 狠/很 in middle-to-late Qing usage. This is the authors’ account, not a settled or independently verified chronology; the page says full text requires CNKI access.
evidence.title: 现代汉语程度副词“很”的来源及演变

It is a modern vector redraw, not a photograph or facsimile of an ancient artifact. The page labels the ancient-script representation public domain; confirm the file’s licensing details on its page when reusing.

search_audit.outcome: Search performed. Opened and inspected the ZDIC page, the English Wiktionary entry, and the 2024 journal article page. The Shuowen small-seal label, phonetic analysis, and competing adverb-origin proposal were available. No usable early oracle-bone/bronze form or independently inspected dated Yuan primary witness was established.

search_audit.outcome: Search performed. Inspected the Commons page for 艮-seal.svg; its description identifies a Shuowen seal-style modern vector rendering and its licensing information. Search results did not establish a reusable Commons image depicting 很 itself.

gaps: No directly inspected oracle-bone, bronze, or Warring States form for 很 was found. The checked graphic evidence reaches the Shuowen small-seal reference only; neither a full earlier graphic sequence nor a corruption or replacement history is established.

The evidence supports 彳 as the semantic component and 艮 as a sound component. It does not establish 彳’s precise semantic contribution to the earliest senses, or a semantic derivation from 艮’s original referent. The pronunciation match supports the component’s phonetic role without requiring recovery of 艮’s oldest depicted object or name.

The early transmitted-text examples available through the inspected dictionary are not direct manuscript witnesses. Their traditional work dates do not establish when the particular wording entered the text.

The move from defiance, querulousness, or cruelty to degree adverb is disputed. The 2024 Yuan-contact account is an article abstract; competing grammaticalization explanations and first-use dating cannot be settled from the inspected materials. The Yuan example and its exact textual witness remain unverified here.

The search did not establish an image of 很 with checked reuse provenance. The proposed Commons image is of its sound component 艮 and is explicitly a modern redraw in a seal-script style, not an ancient artifact image.
